label: Freelancer or solo consultant
profile: A freelancer or solo consultant who sells their own time or expertise directly to clients, project by project or on retainer, rather than a course, a membership or a product sold to a wider audience.

layers.role: A professional portfolio and service site
layers.why: Squarespace's templates are built to look like a finished, designed site on day one, which matters most when the site itself is the pitch. Every current plan allows up to 1,000 pages and unlimited bandwidth, so a portfolio, case studies and a handful of service pages never force an upgrade on their own; only adding a second person to edit the site does.

alternatives.when: You want the cheapest published price for a bare portfolio and don't plan to invoice or take payment through the site itself.
The site has to read as a design portfolio rather than a service brochure, and you're fine handling invoicing somewhere else.

layers.why: Squarespace's built-in invoicing tool sends a real, payable invoice with no Squarespace fee on any plan, so getting paid doesn't need a second subscription or a second login on top of the site you already pay for.

alternatives.when: You sell a fixed-price package or a paid consultation slot through a funnel rather than custom, itemized invoices, and want a free plan with no transaction fee.

layers.role: Track leads, proposals and client relationships
layers.why: Zoho CRM's free plan tracks leads, deals and follow-up reminders for up to three users with no card required, and covers individual, one-to-one emails, which is how a consulting pipeline actually runs. That's different from the bulk marketing email that pushes most CRMs onto a paid plan.

alternatives.when: Sending a proposal the client can sign online is core to how you close deals, and you're willing to pay for a dedicated pipeline app plus its e-signature add-on to get that.

solo.note: Zoho's Free plan (no card required) already covers one person: contact and deal tracking, follow-up reminders and workflow automation, with individual emails covered up to 50 a day. A solo consultant's outreach is one-to-one, not the bulk marketing email that forces most CRM sizings onto a paid plan.

small.note: Still Free: its 3-user cap covers you plus two contractors, and one-to-one client follow-up still doesn't need Standard's Mass Email feature.

growing.note: Five seats on Standard, priced per user at Zoho's list rate: Free's hard cap is exactly 3 users with no way to add a 4th, so a five-person studio has to move up on seats alone, not because it suddenly needs Standard's bulk-email tools.

layers.why: Notion is free and unlimited in pages and blocks for a single-person workspace, which fits a solo consultant's client notes, proposal drafts and SOPs without a task-board structure you don't need yet.

alternatives.when: You're assigning tasks and deadlines to a contractor rather than just sharing docs and notes.

small.note: 3 seats on Plus, at Notion's listed per-member rate: Free becomes limited for any workspace with 2 or more members, and Notion doesn't publish the exact cap, so Plus is the safer buy the moment a contractor joins the workspace.

growing.note: 5 seats on Plus, at the same per-member rate: Plus has no published seat cap, so a five-person studio doesn't need Business unless it wants Notion's full AI agent, SAML SSO or private teamspaces.

extras.name: LinkedIn
extras.note: Free professional profile most B2B clients check before they ever reach your site; keep it pointed at the same portfolio your site shows.

extras.name: Google Search Console
extras.note: Free. Shows which searches already bring visitors to your site and flags indexing problems before they cost you a lead.

skip.what: An agency-built CRM like GoHighLevel or HubSpot Professional
skip.why: Both are priced and designed for a team running campaigns across many clients' accounts at once. A solo consultant's own pipeline is a fraction of that job, and a free CRM already covers it.

skip.what: A separate invoicing or accounting app
skip.why: Your site's own invoicing tool already sends a payable, professional invoice with no platform fee. Adding a stand-alone invoicing app on top means paying for, and re-entering client details into, the same job twice.
A referral-driven consulting practice doesn't run mass email campaigns the way a marketing business does, so a paid sender is overhead until you actually have a list worth mailing on a real schedule.

skip.what: An ecommerce platform like Shopify or WooCommerce
skip.why: Both are built for a product catalog, inventory and shipping. Selling your own time or a project doesn't need a shopping cart, and their fee structure and setup both assume physical goods moving through it.
